questions.prompt: A non-developer operations analyst needs Claude to review a set of local policy files, produce a proposed summary, and save a draft to a chosen folder. The analyst should inspect changes before anything is sent externally. Which entry point best fits the stated work?

options.text: Claude Code as the default engineering shell for a task that requires no code or developer workflow.
Cowork, with the analyst supervising file access and reviewing the saved draft before sharing it.
A customer-facing API integration with automatic external delivery.
A server-side agent with broad filesystem and email permissions and no user checkpoint.

feedback.reason: The scenario centers on a knowledge worker’s local file task with a review checkpoint; select the entry point designed for that non-developer workflow.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Cowork is a distinct entry point oriented to non-developer work with files and tasks; it is not the same choice as a code-centric tool or a product API.
details.scenarioApplication: The scenario centers on a knowledge worker’s local file task with a review checkpoint; select the entry point designed for that non-developer workflow.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The user must confirm what files and actions the specific setup allows; a draft save does not authorize external distribution.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternatives change a different layer, leave the stated risk uncontrolled, or claim more evidence than the scenario supplies.
details.transfer: Choose an entry point that matches the user and work, then keep consequential actions visible and reviewed.

questions.prompt: A project coordinator wants Claude to reorganize a folder of meeting notes and overwrite the originals automatically. The organization requires reversible file changes and human approval. What should the coordinator do?

options.text: Grant full folder access and rely on the assistant to infer which notes are safe to replace.
Use an API call to overwrite the files, then ask the coordinator to review the audit log.
Use a supervised workflow that limits the selected files, creates proposed or reversible changes, and requires the coordinator to inspect before replacing originals.
Move the files into a shared folder so all employees can review the result after overwrite.

feedback.reason: The requirement is supervised reversible file handling; broad automatic overwrite violates the stated approval boundary.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The entry point does not eliminate the need to set scope and review potentially destructive file actions.
details.scenarioApplication: The requirement is supervised reversible file handling; broad automatic overwrite violates the stated approval boundary.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A backup or undo path reduces recovery cost but does not replace required approval before a destructive action.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternatives change a different layer, leave the stated risk uncontrolled, or claim more evidence than the scenario supplies.
details.transfer: Use file scope and checkpoints that match the reversibility and impact of the action.

questions.prompt: A non-technical user asks Claude to summarize local contracts and prepare an email draft. Contracts include documents from external counterparties that may contain instructions addressed to an AI. What is the safer work pattern?

options.text: Let the documents define the email workflow because the counterparties wrote them.
Give Cowork access to the entire drive so it can locate every related contract and send the message when done.
Treat the contract text as trusted instructions if the file came from a known counterparty.
Limit access to the selected files, treat their contents as untrusted data, prepare a draft, and let the user verify the content and recipients before sending.

feedback.reason: External document content is evidence to analyze, not authority to change the task or authorize side effects.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The user-facing workflow should preserve task intent and explicit approval for outbound actions.
details.scenarioApplication: External document content is evidence to analyze, not authority to change the task or authorize side effects.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A known sender does not make all embedded instructions trustworthy; review the proposed summary and recipients.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternatives change a different layer, leave the stated risk uncontrolled, or claim more evidence than the scenario supplies.
details.transfer: Separate document analysis from authority to send or change data.

questions.prompt: An organization is piloting a new local-work entry point with analysts. The team needs to learn whether the workflow is useful without giving every user broad access on day one. What pilot plan is most defensible?

options.text: Select a small representative cohort, define the folders/actions in scope, measure task outcomes and support issues, and expand only after reviewing permissions and user feedback.
Enable full-drive access for the whole organization and use monthly usage volume as the success measure.
Keep the pilot limited to enthusiasts and treat positive comments as evidence that all departments are ready.
Disable all user review checkpoints so the team can measure maximum automation potential.

feedback.reason: A bounded pilot gives evidence on utility and operational friction while limiting exposure and support burden.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Rollout design should pair a representative cohort with scoped access and measures tied to task outcomes.
details.scenarioApplication: A bounded pilot gives evidence on utility and operational friction while limiting exposure and support burden.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A pilot cannot establish readiness for every workflow; expand based on the domains and permissions actually evaluated.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternatives change a different layer, leave the stated risk uncontrolled, or claim more evidence than the scenario supplies.
details.transfer: Scale access and adoption based on evidence, not account activation or enthusiasm alone.
